2.4 Groupoids

A category is called a groupoid if all its morphisms are invertible. In the synthetic setting, we need to phrase this condition for arbitrary terms of the arrow category, as follows.

Definition 2.4.1 (Groupoid). We say that a category \(C\) is a groupoid if in an arbitrary categorical context, every morphism expression \(f\colon x \to y\) in \(C\) is an isomorphism. Explicitly: for every category \(\Gamma \) and every functor \(f\colon \Gamma \to \Ar (C)\), there exists a dashed arrow \(\tilde {f}\) making the following diagram commute:

iso-section-to-identity-section

Derivation, checked

iso-section-to-identity-section : {C : CAT} →
  Section (isoArrow {C}) → Section (identityArrow {C})
Proof / implementation
iso-section-to-identity-section {C} h = record
  { section = j ∘ s
  ; comparison = Section.comparison h ∙
      ((isoArrow ◁ (comp-unitˡ s ∙ ((ε ▷ s) ∙ (comp-assoc s j identityIso) ⁻¹))) ∙
      (comp-assoc (j ∘ s) identityIso isoArrow ∙
        (identityIso-arrow ⁻¹ ▷ (j ∘ s)))) }
  where
  s = Section.section h
  j = IsEquiv.inverse (rezk-isEquiv C)
  ε = (IsEquiv.retractionIso (rezk-isEquiv C)) ⁻¹

(1)

The category \(X\) is a groupoid;

(2)

The functor \(\pi _{\Iso }\colon \Iso (X) \to \Ar (X)\) admits a section, in the sense of Definition 1.3.2;

(3)

The functor \(p_{[1]}^*\colon X \to \Ar (X)\), induced by the map \(p_{[1]}\colon [1] \to *\), admits a section;

(4)

The functor \(p_{[1]}^*\colon X \to \Ar (X)\) is an equivalence.

Proof

Proof. To see that (1) implies (2), take \(\Gamma = \Ar (X)\) and let \(f = \id _{\Ar (X)}\), so that \(s = \tilde {f}\) provides a section. Conversely, if \(s\colon \Ar (X) \to \Iso (X)\) is a section of \(\pi _{\Iso }\), a lift \(\tilde {f}\) of \(f\) may be given as \(\tilde {f} := s \circ f\).

Example 2.4.5. If \(X\) and \(Y\) are groupoids, then their product \(X \times Y\) is a groupoid. This is an immediate consequence of Lemma 1.7.10.

Agda Products of groupoids

product-isGroupoid

Derivation, checked

product-isGroupoid : {C D : CAT} → IsGroupoid C → IsGroupoid D → IsGroupoid (C × D)
Proof / implementation
product-isGroupoid {C} {D} ec ed = equiv-cancel-left identityArrow A.forward A.forward-isEquiv
  (equiv-transport (comparison ⁻¹) (productMap-isEquiv identityArrow identityArrow ec ed))
  where
  module A = ProductComparison [1] C D
  comparison : (A.forward ∘ identityArrow) =₁ (productMap (identityArrow {C}) (identityArrow {D}))
  comparison = pair-cong (constant-natural [1] pr₁) (constant-natural [1] pr₂) ∙
    pair-pre (funPost pr₁) (funPost pr₂) identityArrow

Lemma 2.4.6. Let \(C \to D\) be an equivalence of categories. Then \(C\) is a groupoid if and only if \(D\) is a groupoid.

Agda Invariance under equivalence

equivalence-preserves-groupoid

Derivation, checked

equivalence-preserves-groupoid : {C D : CAT} (f : MAP C D) →
  IsEquiv f → IsGroupoid C → IsGroupoid D
Proof / implementation
equivalence-preserves-groupoid f ef ec = equiv-cancel-right f identityArrow ef
  (equiv-transport (constant-natural [1] f)
    (equiv-compose identityArrow (funPost f) ec (funPost-isEquiv f ef)))

Lemma 2.4.8. Groupoids are closed under retracts: if \(X\) is a groupoid and \(Y\) is a retract of \(X\), then \(Y\) is also a groupoid.

Agda Retracts of groupoids

retract-isGroupoid

Derivation, checked

retract-isGroupoid : {X Y : CAT} (s : MAP Y X) (r : MAP X Y) →
  (r ∘ s) =₁ (id Y) → IsGroupoid X → IsGroupoid Y
Proof / implementation
retract-isGroupoid {X} {Y} s r ε ex = identity-section-to-groupoid
  (record { section = r ∘ (j ∘ funPost s) ; comparison = counit })
  where
  j = IsEquiv.inverse ex
  counit : (identityArrow ∘ (r ∘ (j ∘ funPost s))) =₁ (id (Ar Y))
  counit = funPost-id [1] Y ∙ (funPost-cong ε ∙ (funPost-comp s r ∙
    ((funPost r ◁ (comp-unitˡ (funPost s) ∙
      (((IsEquiv.retractionIso ex) ⁻¹ ▷ funPost s) ∙
        (comp-assoc (funPost s) j identityArrow) ⁻¹))) ∙
    (comp-assoc (j ∘ funPost s) identityArrow (funPost r) ∙
      (((constant-natural [1] r) ⁻¹ ▷ (j ∘ funPost s)) ∙
        (comp-assoc (j ∘ funPost s) r identityArrow) ⁻¹)))))

Proof

Proof. If \(Y\) is a retract of \(X\), then the functor \(Y \to \Ar (Y)\) is a retract of the functor \(X \to \Ar (X)\). In particular, if the latter is an equivalence then so is the former by Lemma 1.3.9. □

Lemma 2.4.9. Consider functors \(f\colon X \to C\) and \(g\colon Y \to C\) and assume that \(X\) and \(Y\) are groupoids. Then the pullback \(X \times _C Y\) is a groupoid.

pullback-isGroupoid : {X Y C : CAT} (f : MAP X C) (g : MAP Y C) →
  IsGroupoid X → IsGroupoid Y → IsGroupoid (Pullback f g)
Proof / implementation
pullback-isGroupoid = PullbackGroupoid.isGroupoid

Proof

Proof. The functor \(X \times _C Y \to \Ar (X \times _C Y)\) factors as \[ X \times _C Y \iso X \times _{\Ar (C)} Y \iso \Ar (X) \times _{\Ar (C)} \Ar (Y) \simeq \Ar (X \times _C Y). \] Here the second functor is an equivalence since \(X\) and \(Y\) are groupoids. The last equivalence is Lemma 1.7.11. Finally, we claim that the first functor is a pullback of the diagonal of the embedding \(i\colon C \to \Ar (C)\) from Corollary 2.3.7 and hence is an equivalence. To see this, consider the following commutative diagram:

The right bottom square, the right outer rectangle and the top outer rectangle are pullback squares by Lemma 1.6.13. It thus follows from Lemma 1.6.11 that also the top left square is a pullback square. □

Lemma 2.4.10. Consider a pullback square

Agda Pullback squares of groupoids

pullback-square-isGroupoid

Derivation, checked

pullback-square-isGroupoid : {X Y C T : CAT} {f : MAP X C} {g : MAP Y C}
  (s : Cone f g T) → IsPullback s → IsGroupoid X → IsGroupoid Y → IsGroupoid T
Proof / implementation
pullback-square-isGroupoid {f = f} {g} s es ex ey =
  equivalence-reflects-groupoid (pullbackLift s) es (pullback-isGroupoid f g ex ey)
